[KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:40:55/r2] KURANYOLU-TEFSIR · author | holds | Revealed during Mecca's most difficult days, the passage assures Muhammad and his community that the promise will come true, as it did for Moses and his followers.
[KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:40:55/r3] KURANYOLU-TEFSIR · author | holds | The command to seek forgiveness predates the Fath promise of forgiveness; using it to date these surahs is invalid because the later Nasr surah also commands the Prophet to seek pardon. | mentions 48:1, 48:2, 48:3, 48:4, 48:5, 48:6, 48:7, 110:3
[KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:40:55/r4] KURANYOLU-TEFSIR · Müfessirler | reports | Some say seeking forgiveness concerns the Prophet's pre-prophethood errors or addresses his community through him, since prophets are protected from sin.
[KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:40:55/r5] KURANYOLU-TEFSIR · author | rejects | The Prophet should not be exempted from the command: repentance and seeking forgiveness are acts of worship, and he swore that he sought forgiveness seventy or one hundred times daily. | mentions 48:1, 48:2, 48:3, 48:4, 48:5, 48:6, 48:7
[KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:40:55/r6] KURANYOLU-TEFSIR · author | reports | Sound reports say the Prophet swore he sought forgiveness seventy or one hundred times each day.
[KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:40:55/r7] KURANYOLU-TEFSIR · Müfessirler | reports | Some interpret morning and evening glorification as the afternoon and dawn prayers, or as two prayer times before the five daily prayers became obligatory.
[KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:40:55/r8] KURANYOLU-TEFSIR · İbn Âşûr | prefers | The verse is not about the obligation or times of prayer; as in Nasr, it simply commands praise, glorification, and seeking forgiveness. | mentions 110:3
[STUDYQURAN:40:55/r1] STUDYQURAN · author | holds | The verse addresses Muhammad and counsels patience, implying he will triumph over his adversaries as Moses and earlier prophets did.
[STUDYQURAN:40:55/r2] STUDYQURAN · Ṭs | reports | The true promise may mean God's aid in this world and reward in the Hereafter.
[STUDYQURAN:40:55/r3] STUDYQURAN · author | reports | Alternatively, the promise may refer specifically to the promise of aid in verses 51–52. | mentions 40:51, 40:52
[STUDYQURAN:40:55/r4] STUDYQURAN · those who maintain that prophets do commit minor sins | reports | For those who hold that prophets can commit minor sins, asking forgiveness means repenting for those sins.
[STUDYQURAN:40:55/r5] STUDYQURAN · majority of Muslims | reports | The majority hold prophets protected from sin; the command instead urges worship and supplication so God may raise Muhammad's rank and make his practice an example for later people.
[STUDYQURAN:40:55/r6] STUDYQURAN · Bḍ | reports | Eventide and dawn mean sunset and the time before sunrise; before the five prayers were instituted in Mecca, two prayer cycles were required in each period.
[STUDYQURAN:40:55/r7] STUDYQURAN · Q | reports | Another interpretation takes eventide and dawn as the night prayer, ʿishāʾ, and the morning prayer, fajr.
[STUDYQURAN:40:intro/r3] STUDYQURAN · Other commentators | reports | Others extend the Madinan classification to verse 55 as well.
[STUDYQURAN:40:intro/r4] STUDYQURAN · Still other commentators | reports | Still others classify only verse 55 as Madinan, interpreting its dawn and eventide praise as morning and sunset prayers, made obligatory only in the last Makkan years.
[STUDYQURAN:40:intro/r9] STUDYQURAN · author | holds | Divine aid to messengers ends with condemnation of those too arrogant to worship God, then transitions to God’s power over creation.
